finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get and returns the response body. An attacker can make the server request arbitrary URLs, including internal services, localhost and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The response is relayed in full, so this is not blind SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the body copied to the response by io.Copy at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch is registered to the fetch handler
target is read from the query string without any processing
http.Get(target) issues the outbound request to the attacker-chosen URL
The response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP validation. The `allowed` map is only used in safeFetch, not in fetch. No private-range blocking and no custom transport or dialer. The default client follows redirects.

verdict.reason: main.go:15 reads `target` from the query string and main.go:16 passes it to http.Get with no validation (the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch at main.go:27), and main.go:22 streams the body back; /fetch is registered at main.go:41 with no auth middleware.
